name: Calculator
description: This project develops a smartphone app for a simple calculator. In its initial version, it allows the user to do basic calculations. More complex calculations will be considered in subsequent versions that are added iteratively.
rawDescription: This project develops a smartphone app for a simple calculator. In its initial version, it allows the user to do basic calculations. More complex calculations will be considered in subsequent versions that are added iteratively.
highLevelGoals: Enable users to perform fundamental arithmetic operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
lowLevelGoals: The user enters the first operand for the calculation.
The user selects an arithmetic operation (addition, subtraction, multiplication, or division) from the available options.
The user enters the second operand for the calculation.
The user presses the equals button to execute the selected operation on the two operands.
The system displays the computed result of the operation on the screen.

baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The high-level goals are correctly aligned with the software description, focusing solely on functional requirements for a basic calculator app. No contradictions or omissions are present, and the goals are clear and representative of the system's purpose.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals are well-defined, functional, and directly correspond to the user's actions for performing basic calculations. They cover all necessary steps from inputting numbers to displaying the result, aligning perfectly with the high-level goal of enabling fundamental arithmetic operations.

hlg_342521cf6fdd0795_001.rationale: llg_001 enables user input of the first operand; llg_002 enables selection of an arithmetic operation (addition, subtraction, multiplication, or division); llg_003 enables user input of the second operand; llg_004 triggers the calculation based on the selected operation and operands; llg_005 displays the computed result. Together, these form a complete sequence for performing and displaying a single arithmetic operation on two operands, with no inferred or omitted functionality.
